notes: Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science 5 (2002) 47-54. READ IN FULL 21 September 2026 from the journal PDF at literature/sources/monks-2002-3x1-minus-the-plus-dmtcs-5-47-54.pdf. The earlier record said dmtcs.episciences.org was egress-blocked 'as is every other route tried'; it answered 200 on 21 September. Kenneth G. Monks, Department of Mathematics, University of Scranton; received Aug 10 2001, accepted April 9 2002. THEOREM 1: there are INFINITELY MANY functions R(n) = r_i n for n = i mod d, with r_i rational, such that the 3x+1 conjecture holds if and only if the R-orbit of 2^n contains 2 for every positive n; the explicit witness is the Fractran rule (1/11, 136/15, 5/17, 4/5, 26/21, 7/13, 1/7, 33/4, 5/2, 7) with d = 1021020. Furthermore the R-orbit of 2^n contains 2^n, 2^T(n), 2^(T^2(n)), ... and no other powers of two. THEOREM 2: the R-orbit of an arbitrary positive integer is a constant multiple of an orbit containing a power of 2. COROLLARY 1 IS THE PART THAT MATTERS HERE: any cycle {x_0, ..., x_(m-1)} of positive integers for the 3x+1 function satisfies sum_{i in E} floor(x_i / 2) = sum_{i in O} floor(x_i / 2) + k, with O the odd indices, E the even, k = |O|. That is a FLOOR IDENTITY ON A CYCLE derived from an addition-free rewriting of the map, which is structurally the shape the Juggler cycle branches keep producing; whether it is more than a restatement of the cycle equation is NOT CLAIMED and must be checked before anyone says so. knight-2026-small-collatz-rule re-derives the same identity from his own coefficient system and calls it well known. THE STATED METHOD, which is the reusable part: 'a general mechanism for deriving mathematical results about the iterative dynamics of arbitrary integer functions from Fractran algorithms'. THE COMPARISON THIS REGISTER OPENED REMAINS OPEN. Monks and Knight buy the removal of the +1 by ENLARGING THE STATE SPACE (a million conditions, then thirty); the Juggler buys it by MOVING TO THE EXPONENT and paying a floor. Which trade is cheaper, and whether the two constructions meet, is still a comparison this laboratory has not made -- but it is now a comparison between two texts that have both been read.
